## Things I Think We Want

- Knowledge database: papers, abstracts, notes, linked and semantically searchable, bibliographic data (bibfile or other)
- Team of agents per project: project direction, literature search, data analysis, project redirection, writing, referee report (actor-critic for each task)
- Logs: "What did my coauthors do last week?",  "Why did we change that?"

## Knowledge Databases {.section-divider}

## What Do We Want?

::: {.card .card-blue}
- A local, private store of PDFs, abstracts, and notes
- Full-text keyword *and* semantic (meaning) search
- Import PDFs, a folder of PDFs, web search results, Zotero 
- Notes tied to the papers that prompted them
- Export BibTeX 
:::

## Three Storage Types

::: {.three-cards}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[Relational (SQL)]{.card-title}

- The facts: title, authors, year, DOI, citekey, reading status, project tag
- Exact filters and joins --- "unread, 2020 or later, this project"
- Keyword search lives here too --- [BM25]{.accent} over the full text
:::
::: {.card .card-amber}
[Vector]{.card-title}

- Meaning, not wording --- finds the paper when you don't recall the author's vocabulary
- Passages get embedded, so a hit returns the paper [and the page]{.accent}
- Your own notes embed here, alongside the papers
:::
::: {.card .card-teal}
[Graph]{.card-title}

- Who cites whom --- edges, not rows
- Trace a result forward to its critics and back to its roots
- The query it unlocks: what my library leans on that I [don't own yet]{.accent}
:::
:::



## LitDB: All in One SQlite Database


::: {.card .card-green}


- Ordinary tables for papers, notes, passages, projects
- SQLite's own full-text index for keyword search
- Every chunk compared on every query; cosine similarity is one matrix multiplication
- Citations as an edge table, queried with joins
- No server, no extension, nothing to keep running
:::

Perfectly fine (according to Claude) for a research corpus of a few thousand papers.  



## Notes {.shrink}

Whatever format you like.  Plain text is fine. Tell Claude: "add <filename> to litdb"
Claude will read and try to classify.

::: {.card-amber}
- Kind --- idea, summary, critique, question, todo, or quote
- Which paper in your library it is about, by searching for it
- How it relates to that paper --- about, supports, contradicts, extends, uses-method, uses-data
- The page or the verbatim quote it points at
- Project tag --- defaults to the folder you are working in
- Whether it is confidential --- unpublished ideas and referee material are embedded locally, never sent to an API
:::

::: {.explainer}
It says what it filed, so you can correct a guess you never had to make
:::

## Finding Papers You Don't Have {.shrink}

::: {.two-cards}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[Where it looks]{.card-title}

- Your own library first, always
- Then [OpenAlex]{.accent} (free, no key) and [Semantic Scholar]{.accent}
- Every hit says whether you already have it
- Or work the citation graph: this paper's references, who cites it, what your library leans on that you don't own
:::
::: {.card .card-amber}
[What lands in the database]{.card-title}

- Bibliographic data --- authors, year, venue, DOI --- and a citekey for your `.bib`
- The abstract, indexed and embedded like any other text
- Then Claude goes after the PDF: open-access copy, arXiv/SSRN/NBER, the author's page
- No PDF? The abstract still makes the paper findable by meaning
:::
:::


## When the Paper Is Behind a Paywall {.shrink}

::: {.card .card-blue}
[Claude can drive your own browser]{.card-title}

- `claude --chrome` --- the Claude in Chrome extension, sharing the login state you already have
- You sign in to the library proxy; Claude pauses at login pages and CAPTCHAs and hands the keyboard back
- Then it carries on: find the PDF, download it, ingest it into the record that already exists
- Alternatives: [Playwright]{.accent} (an MCP server --- works, but its own browser profile, so you sign in again there), or [Cowork]{.accent}, which is this in a Chrome side panel and no terminal
:::

::: {.explainer}
One paper you are entitled to, fetched through your own subscription, is ordinary use. Scripted bulk downloading is not --- it violates publisher terms and gets the campus IP range cut off. Claude is instructed never to touch Sci-Hub.
:::


## Comparisons

::: {.comparison-table}

| | litdb | NotebookLM | Obsidian | Zotero |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Where it lives | Your disk | Google's cloud | Your disk | Your disk + their cloud |
| Searches full PDF text | Yes | Within one notebook | Only with plugins | Yes, keyword |
| Search by meaning | Yes | Yes | Plugin | No |
| Citation graph | Yes | No | The links you drew, not citations | No |
| Writes a `.bib` | Yes | No | Plugin | Yes |
| Driven by | Claude, in chat | Its own web UI | You, by hand | You, by hand |

:::

## Research Agents {.section-divider}

## What We Want

::: {.four-cards}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[Guidance]{.card-title}

"I have an idea.  What do you think?" to "How deeply should I go into X?"
:::
::: {.card .card-amber}
[Data analysis]{.card-title}

Pull data, analyze, figures, tables
:::
::: {.card .card-teal}
[Writing]{.card-title}

"Write a draft of the data section", "Edit the introduction", ...
:::


::: {.card .card-purple}
[Review]{.card-title}
From "check that the numbers in the text match the tables" to "give me a full referee report"
:::
:::

## Actor-Critic


::: {.two-cards}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[Actor]{.card-title}

- Produces the thing: the idea, the sample, the paragraph
- Charged with being generative and specific, not with being right
- Optimized to make something exist
:::
::: {.card .card-amber}
[Critic]{.card-title}

- Charged with finding what is wrong with it
- Has its own standard of "good" and its own charter --- not "check this over"
- Every objection must name the [check that would settle it]{.accent}
:::
:::

::: {.explainer}
Ask one agent to draft and then review, and it reviews the thing it just decided was good. The two jobs have to be separate calls with separate instructions --- and the more independent the critic, the more it catches.
:::


## Agent Teams

::: {.four-cards}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[Guidance]{.card-title}

A proposer comes up with ideas, and adversaries shoot them down
:::
::: {.card .card-amber}
[Data analysis]{.card-title}

Analyst and replicator build the sample independently, and must agree before analysis starts
:::
::: {.card .card-teal}
[Writing]{.card-title}

Read from different angles: accuracy, persuasion, devil's advocate
:::
::: {.card .card-purple}
[Review]{.card-title}

Multiple independent reports
:::
:::

## How to Get Independent Views

::: {.three-cards}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[Subagents]{.card-title}

Ask Claude to generate them.  A subagent starts fresh with instructions from the main agent.

It does not see the conversation history --- which is the whole point.
:::
::: {.card .card-amber}
[Different models]{.card-title}

Sonnet, Opus, Fable for different seats.

Different capability, but still correlated priors --- they were trained by the same people.
:::
::: {.card .card-teal}
[Different families]{.card-title}

Claude can call ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, ...

Genuinely different blind spots.  Uses your API keys (and your credit card).
:::
:::


## The research Plugin {.shrink}

It starts with a quiz.  Empirical or theory?  Who are the coauthors?  Where does the data live?  A debate panel?  Does anyone write in Overleaf?

Then it sets up only what you said yes to:

::: {.card .card-blue}
- [Folder structure]{.accent} --- a place of your own, and a shared place that is the project
- [Data location]{.accent} --- outside the repo, wherever you already keep it
- How to run [Guidance, Data analysis, Writing, and Review]{.accent}
- [Memory]{.accent} --- what gets written down, and when
:::

::: {.explainer}
All of it codified in two documents.  `CLAUDE.md` is the operating manual, and Claude reads it at the start of every session.  `protocols.html` is the same project explained to a person --- what a coauthor reads on their first day.
:::


## Overleaf and the Git Bridge {.shrink}

::: {.card .card-blue}
[For teams where only some coauthors use Overleaf]{.card-title}

- `draft/` alone is mirrored to an Overleaf project --- `tools/`, `workspaces/`, `project/` never go there
- Coauthors who do not use Overleaf change [nothing]{.accent}; the repo stays the source of truth
- One person runs the bridge: `git subtree pull`, then `git subtree push`
- Always pull before pushing --- Overleaf rejects non-fast-forward pushes and forbids `--force` outright
:::

::: {.explainer}
Wire it before anyone starts commenting. Renaming a file destroys Overleaf's comment anchors, so the file hygiene --- naming the paper `main.tex`, untracking build noise --- is cheaper now than it will ever be again.
:::

## Slash Commands

::: {.comparison-table}

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/research:setup` | The interview, then builds or restructures the repo |
| `/round` | Finishes a round --- writes what you took up and what came of it, and promotes whatever settled |
| `/round start` | Optional.  Claims the round when a coauthor might be working right now |
| `/refresh` | Context is getting long: writes your handoff and stops, so you can `/clear`.  Keeps the round open |
| `/report` | An HTML report: executive summary, what is settled, open issues, chronology |
| `/critique` | The reviewer panel and the paths forward |
| `/econ-review` | Referee-grade report, if installed |
| litdb | No command --- just ask, in plain language |

:::

## Get Started {.shrink}

- Tell Claude to install the plugin research@kerryback (install the marketplace github.com/kerryback/skills first if you haven't).
- Start a new conversation in the folder you want the project in.  Ask Claude how to use the research skill.
- Then `/research:setup`.

::: {.three-cards}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[Empty folder]{.card-title}

Answers the eight questions, then builds only what you said yes to
:::
::: {.card .card-amber}
[A repo that already has work]{.card-title}

Asks what is live and what is superseded, then restructures in order --- paths, then data out, then per-author folders, then archive.  Commits between steps
:::
::: {.card .card-teal}
[A repo it already set up]{.card-title}

Nothing to invoke.  `CLAUDE.md` is in the folder, so a new conversation reads it and picks up where the last one stopped
:::
:::

::: {.explainer}
The third case is the normal one.  You run setup once; after that you just start talking, and the rules travel with the repo rather than with you.
:::

## WRDS {.section-divider}

## Getting Data from WRDS

::: {.three-cards}
::: {.card-blue}
Claude can write and run Python scripts to pull data from WRDS
:::
::: {.card-amber}
Needs your username and password (password in .pgpass file, username in scripts)
::: 
::: {.card-teal}
Uses `wrds` Python library.  Install it with no-deps option, because otherwise it will downgrade pandas and break things.
:::
:::

Ask Claude to install wrds@kerryback.  

::: {.two-cards}
::: {.card-purple}
Contains Python scripts from WRDS, scripts from OpenAssetPricing (Chen & Zimmerman), and variable definitions from French's data library
:::
::: {.card-red}
Contains SKILL.md: install wrds with no-deps option; warn user if a variable is requested and WRDS, Chen-Zimmerman, and Fama-French define it differently
:::
:::

## Use Claude on jgsrc1 {.section-divider}

## Remote SSH

- Upgrade Academic Studio to 1.2 (Help -> Check for updates)
- Academic Studio (or VS Code): Settings (bottom left) -> Command Palette -> Remote SSH Connect to Host 
- Create host profile: Host = jgsrc1@rice.edu, User = <netid>
- Connect.  Prompted for password.  Open a folder.  Prompted for password again

## One-Time Install

- You need to install the Claude Code extension and other extensions that need to live on the remote machine.

- You need a Python environment.  There are options.  I recommend the following

::: {.card-dark}
[Prompt]{.card-title}
Install uv.  Use uv to create a Python 3.14 venv.  Install the data analysis stack.  Install wrds with the no-deps option.  Write a CLAUDE.md to always use the venv.
:::
